body: FedRAMP is moving cloud authorization packages to OSCAL — the Open Security Controls Assessment Language — and the 30 September fiscal-year boundary is the milestone when machine-readable, OSCAL-based submission becomes the expected format for new packages. OSCAL is NIST's standard for expressing security controls, system security plans, and assessment results as structured data instead of prose documents, so a system security plan is not a PDF an assessor reads by eye but a machine-readable evidence package. For the Council of AI, the verified measurement credential is the direct input to OSCAL evidence: the 14-axis board measurements, the Ed25519-signed manifests, and the incident timelines from the Council Signal containment index together form a machine-readable evidence set that an OSCAL-based authorization can reference. NIST AI 600-1 provides a profile of the AI RMF 1.0 tailored to generative AI and maps directly onto the FedRAMP OSCAL mandate along three axes — GOVERN (profile governance functions align with security assessment documentation), MEASURE (continuous measurement replaces self-attestation), and MANAGE (incident response and boundary review). The language binds: monitored containment (instrument the boundary, publish timelines, accept no claim of perfect isolation) not provable isolation; verified measurement credential (manifest-bound, independently verifiable, not vendor-asserted). The Council of AI does not claim AUKUS-certified partnership or DAIC certification — those require signed letters on file — but the measurement framework is designed to be compatible with UK-sovereign, EU-sovereign-compatible, and AUKUS-compatible procurement requirements.
